diagnostic_evidence.quote: the orthogonal Tucker factor matrices $V^{(\ell)} G^{(\ell)} \in \R^{n_\ell \times r_\ell^0}$

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed identity cannot hold: $V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)}$ is $n_\ell\times r_\ell^0$ with $r_\ell^0<r_\ell\le n_\ell$, so $V G G^T V^T$ is an $n_\ell\times n_\ell$ matrix of rank at most $r_\ell^0<n_\ell$ and cannot equal $I_{n_\ell}$. The relevant orthonormality is $(VG)^T(VG)=G^TV^TVG=G^TG=I_{r_\ell^0}$, which the proof neither states nor derives; the proof only asserts that substituting the factorization 'proves' orthogonality.

failure_location.quote: proves the orthogonality  $V^{(\ell)} G^{(\ell)} [G^{(\ell)}]^T [V^{(\ell)}]^T =I_{n_\ell}$, which completes the proof.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the identity by $(V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)})^T V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)} = G^{(\ell)T}V^{(\ell)T}V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)} = G^{(\ell)T}G^{(\ell)}=I_{r_\ell^0}$, using orthonormality of the columns of $V^{(\ell)}$ and $G^{(\ell)}$.
issues.overall_effect: The statement of the proposition (orthonormal columns of $V^{(\ell)}G^{(\ell)}$) remains true, but its written proof asserts a false identity and gives no actual argument for the orthogonality claim.
issues.title: Orthogonality identity in proof of Proposition 2.5 is false (wrong product order/dimension)
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction restores a valid proof; the statement and all downstream uses survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The orthogonality property is based on the argument analogues to the  algebraic case but reformulated for polynomial arrays and note that the inner product should be properly weighted.
which forms a sequence of orthogonal polynomials on $[-1,1]$ with respect to the weight $w(x) = 1/\sqrt{1-x^2}$

issues.failure_explanation: The Chebyshev polynomials are $w$-orthogonal but not $w$-orthonormal: $\|T_0\|_w^2=\pi$ while $\|T_k\|_w^2=\pi/2$ for $k\ge1$. Hence for $v_j=\sum_i V_{ij}T_{i-1}$ with Euclidean-orthonormal columns of $V$, $\langle v_j,v_{j'}\rangle_w=\frac{\pi}{2}(\delta_{jj'}+V_{1j}V_{1j'})$, which is nonzero whenever both first-row entries are nonzero. Counterexample: $m=2$, $V=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$ gives $\langle v_1,v_2\rangle_w=\pi/4\ne0$. The 'properly weighted' inner product does not rescue the claim since the $T_0$ normalization mismatch persists. (The statement also refers to $r_\ell^0$ polynomials and to \cref{eqn:beta-Tucker}, while $V^{(\ell)}$ has $r_\ell$ columns and belongs to the decomposition of ${\bf C}$.)

failure_location.quote: If \cref{eqn:beta-Tucker} present the orthogonal Tucker tensor, then $\{T_{0:m_\ell-1}(x_\ell)V^{(\ell)}\}$ appear to be the set of $r_\ell^0$ orthogonal polynomials.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either drop the orthogonality claim or use a $w$-orthonormal basis (rescale $T_0$ by $1/\sqrt2$, i.e., scale the first row of ${\bf C}$/$W^{(\ell)}$ accordingly) before the Tucker decomposition, so that Euclidean orthonormality of $V^{(\ell)}$ transfers to $w$-orthonormality of the factor polynomials.
issues.overall_effect: The orthogonality assertion of Proposition 2.6, advertised as important for further multilinear algebra, is false for the Euclidean-orthogonal factors produced by tuck_als; the conversion formula (2.13) itself is unaffected.
issues.title: Claimed weighted orthogonality of factor polynomials $T_{0:m-1}V^{(\ell)}$ is false
issues.why_classification: A routine local rescaling of the basis (or deletion of the unused side claim) fixes the statement; no other result depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We use the classical Tucker-ALS algorithm in our theoretical analysis
we can approximate the coefficient tensor ${\bf C}$ by a Tucker tensor with almost optimal rank parameter ${\bf r}=(r_1,r_2,r_3)$ using  Tucker-ALS algorithm

issues.failure_explanation: Tucker-ALS (HOOI) is an alternating local optimization for fixed ranks; it has no known guarantee of converging to the best rank-${\bf r}$ approximation nor of producing almost minimal ranks for a prescribed relative error ε. Only the HOSVD initialization provides a quasi-optimality bound (factor $\sqrt{d}$) for fixed ranks. The paper's formal results (Prop. 3.1, Lemma 3.6, Thm 3.7) use only the relative-error inequality, which can be enforced by rank selection, so the 'almost optimal rank' guarantee is asserted but not established or supported by a cited theorem.

failure_location.quote: It enjoys strong theoretical guarantees such that for any given $\varepsilon > 0$, it can approximate the original tensor in the sense of relative error $\|{\bf C} - \hat{\bf C}\|_{\mathrm{F}} \leq \varepsilon\|{\bf C}\|_{\mathrm{F}}$ with almost optimal rank parameters

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the remark to state that Tucker-ALS delivers a Tucker approximation satisfying the prescribed relative error (with HOSVD quasi-optimality for fixed ranks), and describe rank near-optimality as observed numerically rather than guaranteed.
issues.overall_effect: The narrative that the ChebTuck ranks are provably 'almost optimal' rests on an unsupported claim about Tucker-ALS; the numerical evidence stands, but no theoretical optimality of rank follows.
issues.title: Overstated theoretical guarantee of Tucker-ALS (almost optimal ranks for given ε)
issues.why_classification: Only a prose overclaim needs softening; every formal result uses just the relative-error property, which remains valid.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: {\bf C} = {\bf T} \times_1 W^{(1)} \times_2 W^{(2)} \times_3 W^{(3)} = \sum_{k=1}^{R}\xi_k {\bf c}_k^{(1)} \otimes {\bf c}_k^{(2)} \otimes {\bf c}_k^{(3)}

issues.failure_explanation: The RHOSVD estimate $\|{\bf C}-\hat{\bf C}\|_F\le\|\xi\|\sum_\ell(\sum_{k>r_\ell}\sigma_k^{(\ell)2})^{1/2}$ from the cited theorem requires the canonical vectors of the input to be unit vectors (the proof bounds the other-mode factors by their norms, which must be 1). Here the canonical vectors ${\bf c}_k^{(\ell)}=W^{(\ell)}{\bf q}_k^{(\ell)}$ are Chebyshev coefficient vectors of spline interpolants of the normalized ${\bf a}_k^{(\ell)}$ and are in general not normalized, while the weights $\xi_k$ are those of the original CP tensor ${\bf F}$. Thus the lemma's bound, with $\|\xi\|$ and $\sigma_k^{(\ell)}$ as written, is not established; the correct bound involves the rescaled weights $\xi_k\prod_\ell\|{\bf c}_k^{(\ell)}\|$ (or the norms of the side vectors). The singular values $\sigma_k^{(\ell)}$ are also never defined in the statement.

failure_location.quote: The desired result then follows from the standard error analysis of the RHOSVD truncation \cite[Theorem 2.5]{khoromskij2009multigrid}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Normalize ${\bf c}_k^{(\ell)}$, absorbing $\prod_\ell\|{\bf c}_k^{(\ell)}\|$ into new weights $\tilde\xi_k$, define $\sigma_k^{(\ell)}$ as singular values of the normalized side matrices, and restate Lemma 3.6 and Theorem 3.7 with $\|\tilde{\boldsymbol\xi}\|$.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.6 and the second term of Theorem 3.7 are unjustified as stated; the constant in the RHOSVD error term must change.
issues.title: RHOSVD error bound applied without normalized canonical vectors of ${\bf C}$
issues.why_classification: A routine renormalization restores the hypothesis of the cited theorem; the form of the bound and the adaptive-rank remark survive with adjusted constants.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \cref{alg:cheb_tuck_alg}: $C_4 m^3(m+n) + C_5 m^3 + C_1 m^3 \log m + C_2 m^4 + C_3 m^4 |\log \varepsilon|$.
Construct the multivariate cubic spline interpolation $Q(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ of the data ${\bf F}$ on the uniform grid by, e.g., \texttt{interpn} in MATLAB.

issues.failure_explanation: Algorithm 2 constructs a tensor-product cubic spline interpolant of the full data tensor ${\bf F}\in\R^{n_1\times n_2\times n_3}$. Computing the spline coefficients requires a (global, tridiagonal) solve along every grid line in each mode, i.e. at least reading all $n^3$ entries, so the cost is $\Omega(n^3)$ (e.g. $O(n^2(n+m)+mn(n+m)+m^2(n+m))$ if done mode by mode). The claimed $O(m^3(m+n))$ is smaller than $n^3$ whenever $m^3(m+n)<n^3$ (e.g. $m=129$, $n=4096$), so the stated bound is impossible; the proof's 'similarly' extrapolation from the univariate $O(m+n)$ cost is invalid.

failure_location.quote: Similarly, the cost of trivariate cubic spline interpolation which is required in \cref{alg:cheb_tuck_alg} is $\mathcal{O}(m^3(m+n))$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the Algorithm 2 estimate by one containing an $O(n^3)$ (or $O(n^2(n+m))$) term for the trivariate spline construction, with a correct mode-by-mode cost derivation.
issues.overall_effect: The complexity estimate for Algorithm 2 in Proposition 3.8 is false; the grid-size dependence is cubic rather than linear in $n$. The comparative conclusion (Algorithms 3–4 are cheaper) survives, as do the other three estimates.
issues.title: Complexity of Algorithm 2 omits the unavoidable $\Omega(n^3)$ cost of the trivariate spline on the full grid
issues.why_classification: The stated complexity guarantee for one algorithm worsens materially (from linear to cubic in $n$) and needs a corrected argument, but the fix is contained and the paper's main claims rest on Algorithms 3–4, whose estimates are unaffected.
